title: Zooplankton and larval fish on the US Northeast Shelf followed most of their spatial temperature gradient in 1982-2023 (5-year ratios 0.78 and 0.55), several times the bird and network values
abstract: Question: campaign work found that community temperature indices (CTI) follow only 4-24% of their spatial temperature slope in birds, butterflies, river invertebrates and 75 networks. Is this gap general, or does it depend on organism processes such as slow colonisation? Data: NOAA NEFSC EcoMon/MARMAP plankton tows, 1982-2023 (25,753 zooplankton tows, 39 taxon groups; 18,360 tows with fish larvae, 39 taxa), with NOAA OISST v2.1 monthly SST and in situ temperature and salinity. Method: seasonal species thermal indices from the SST climatology at capture sites; spatial slope of 0.5-degree cell CTI on climatological SST; temporal slopes at four timescales with cell x bimonth fixed effects and day-of-year control; joint 3-year and 2-degree block bootstrap; shuffle null; species-level transfer without thermal indices; temperature-salinity models. Results: the spatial slopes were 0.12 (zooplankton) and 0.51 (larval fish) C per C. Relative to these slopes, 5-year CTI changes followed 0.78 (95% CI 0.41-0.92) and 0.55 (0.19-0.73), and 1982-2023 trends 1.71 (0.70-3.61) and 0.92 (0.33-1.25). Year-to-year ratios were 0.45 and 0.37, about ten times the bird value. In EcoMon-only periods (1992-2023, 2000-2023) the ratios were 0.6-1.0; across weights, time-split indices and leave-one-taxon-out they were 0.5-1.9. Species-level slow transfer was 1.47 (0.64-2.85) and 2.04 (0.45-3.73), against 0.14 in birds. The temperature effect stayed with salinity control, and salinity did not trend. The zooplankton shuffle null gave z = 4.5; the larval fish null was marginal (p = 0.053). Conclusion: weak space-for-time transfer is not universal. With Finnish moths, short-generation, highly mobile assemblages approach full transfer, which supports dispersal and demographic limitation as the cause of the gap elsewhere. Limitations: one shelf, survey-internal indices, coarse taxa, surface SST, wide trend intervals, and a cross-study comparison that is not a causal test.

Grey: prior campaign results taken from their abstracts (birds, 75 networks, butterflies with European indices, river invertebrates, Finnish groups). Dashed line: full spatial equivalence.

Plankton tracking ratio by timescale: local tow anomaly, year-to-year anomaly, 5-year means and 1982-2023 trend, with 95% block-bootstrap intervals. Grey band: range of slow fractions for birds and the 75-network synthesis from prior campaign work.

Species-level transfer without thermal indices. Each point is a taxon: observed decadal trend of log density against the trend expected from its spatial SST sensitivity and the SST trend. Line: across-taxon fit with 95% bootstrap interval of the slope; dashed: 1:1.
